# The release-note archive leaves the engine for the content corpus

## Context

`.github/RELEASE_NOTES` holds 169 files: the archive v8.1.0–v13.1.0 plus the pending `v13.2.0.md`. `neomjs/github-content-sync` publishes the same 168 versions under `neo/release-notes`, chunked at 100 (`chunk-1` 100, `chunk-2` 68, `_index.json`). Nothing keeps the two copies equal, and they have drifted: at corpus pin `1152671f7e`, 34 are byte-identical (`v13.1.0.md` among them), 120 differ only in line endings and 14 in content, such as guide links the engine pinned to commits. The flat folder grows by one per release toward GitHub's 1,000-entry directory listing cap. Neo has 1,196 releases, so a backfill would cross that cap at once.

How the copy got here: #19157 chose `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/` as the authored path. #19159 is the operator's call to delete `resources/content`, executed by #19322 on 2026-09-29. It `git mv`'d the chunked archive there flat and made the authored file the archive, while the corpus kept publishing the same notes.

## The Problem

There are two archives and one of them is unguarded. A correction to an old note lands in one copy only. The engine also carries content that the 13.2 split moved out of it.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: the operator, 2026-10-10: *"gut feeling: except for the pending v13.2 release notes, we should remove items from the neo repo"*, followed by the request for this ticket. This supersedes #19159's *"The authored file is the archive; `publish.mjs` reads it there and no longer deletes it after the release."* The authored path stays (#19157). This is aligned with ADR 0004's single corpus with ordinal-100 chunking (`learn/agentos/decisions/0004-github-content-architecture.md`).

The readers of the flat archive at `dev` 5698517f19:

| Reader | Where | Today |
|---|---|---|
| Portal | `apps/portal/neo-config.json:7` `releaseNotesBasePath` | fetches the notes at runtime |
| Release index | `buildScripts/docs/index/release.mjs`, root from `buildScripts/util/contentRoot.mjs:50` `getEngineReleaseNotesRoot` | writes `releases.json` with paths relative to the declared root |
| Index + SEO rebuild | `buildScripts/docs/rebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.mjs:119` `--release-notes <path>` | already takes a declared root |
| Dev server | `buildScripts/webpack/webpack.server.config.mjs:135` | serves the dot-directory |
| Release | `buildScripts/release/publish.mjs:18-19, 93` | authors the note and keeps it as the archive |
| Specs | `PublishReleaseNoteOrphan.spec.mjs:39`, `ReleaseNoteFrontmatter.spec.mjs:34` (reads `v13.1.0.md`), `seo/Generate.spec.mjs:45`, `RebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.spec.mjs:179` | assert the flat archive |
| Pages | `neomjs/pages` `buildScripts/updateNeoVersion.mjs:130-183` (step 4.1) | copies `release-notes` from the engine tag and every other family from the corpus pin |
| Brain KB | neomjs/neo-agent-brain: `ReleaseNotesCorpusSource` reads the corpus; `ai/services/knowledge-base/helpers/coreCorpusProfilePlan.mjs:35` omits the engine-path `ReleaseNotesSource` | expected unchanged; verify |

## The Fix

1. `git rm` v8.1.0–v13.1.0 from `.github/RELEASE_NOTES`. The folder keeps only the pending `v<next>.md`.
2. The archive readers take the corpus root (`neo/release-notes`, chunked, `_index.json`). The pending note still comes from the engine wherever a build needs it before the corpus has it, because the corpus gains a release's note only after the post-release sync.
3. In `publish.mjs` the note stays authored at `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v<version>.md`, and "stays there as the archive" leaves the JSDoc. The previous note leaves the engine in the next release's commit, by version comparison alone: `publish.mjs` never reads the corpus, so the Engine-only boundary holds. Its corpus copy is two separate steps, the content sync archiving its GitHub Release and Pages moving its corpus pin past it (pages README, step 1). *(Restated after review: [5479579324](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19555#pullrequestreview-5479579324).)*
4. Pages step 4.1 (a companion PR in `neomjs/pages`) takes `release-notes` from the corpus pin plus the tag's own note.
5. ADR 0004, `CodebaseOverview.md` and the specs follow the new shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 `.github/RELEASE_NOTES` holds only the pending note.
- [ ] AC-2 The Pages build lists v8.1.0–v13.1.0 plus the pending note, and the Portal renders one archived note. *(Restated at intake: a local engine build has no corpus, so its committed `releases.json` lists the pending note only; the merged list is Pages step 4.1's, AC-4.)* Evidence: the merged note count and the rendered note.
- [ ] AC-3 The release-note steps of `publish.mjs` pass for 13.2.0. Their specs move red→green with the new shape.
- [ ] AC-4 Pages step 4.1 builds from the corpus archive plus the tag's note. The companion PR merges before or with this one.
- [ ] AC-5 `git grep RELEASE_NOTES` is audited, and every remaining hit reads only the pending note.

## Out of Scope

Backfilling the notes before v8.1.0, changing the corpus layout, and the Knowledge Base ingestion path.

## Release relation

The operator would like this before the 13.2 publish. It rides the cut only if AC-1–AC-4 are green before the notes re-review (step 5 of #14800's cut order, [6097885253](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/14800#issuecomment-6097885253)). Otherwise it lands after the publish. It never gates the release.

The engine kept a flat copy of every published release note (168 files,
v8.1.0-v13.1.0) beside the corpus's chunked archive in
neomjs/github-content-sync; v13.1.0 was byte-identical in both, nothing kept
them equal, and the flat folder grew toward GitHub's 1,000-entry listing cap.

The engine now holds only the note being written. publish.mjs drops every
older note in the release commit, since each was published with its GitHub
Release, which the corpus archives. The orphan spec pins that lifecycle and
asserts no note older than package.json's version remains. Links into the
archive move to GitHub Release pages; the committed release index lists the
pending note. The Pages build reads the archive from the corpus (companion).
